steps.title: Open the cockpit
steps.narration: We start at Tapeology's live cockpit — there's nothing to sign into, it's ready immediately.
steps.point_out: Simulated mode is already selected by default, so you can start watching a ticker right away.

steps.title: Watch a simulated ticker
steps.narration: Typing in a simulated ticker and clicking Watch.

steps.title: Simulated chart, honest empty state
steps.narration: The candlestick chart and tape-state markers appear right away for the simulated ticker.
steps.point_out: Directly below the chart, an honest "No tradable map for SIM-BUYER." message shows instead of a fake band — simulated tickers have no real market structure to compare against, and the app says so plainly.

steps.title: Switch to a real historical session
steps.narration: Now switching to Historical mode to replay a real trading session — AAPL testing its own $300 resistance level.

steps.title: Search for AAPL
steps.narration: Typing AAPL into the symbol search.

steps.title: Pick June 22, 2026
steps.narration: Typing in the exact date of the pinned resistance test.

steps.title: Use the market-open preset
steps.narration: One click fills in the correct trading-session time window.

steps.title: Replay the real AAPL session
steps.narration: Clicking Watch replays this real historical session from its very first candle.
steps.point_out: The tradable band overlay is drawn directly on the chart with the correct prior-session basis from the first moment — no flash of today's date first. The chart now waits until it genuinely knows which session it's replaying before it ever asks for bands.

steps.title: Open the Structure page
steps.narration: Moving to the Structure page, where every historical band-touch event is catalogued.

steps.title: Filter Case Studies to AAPL
steps.narration: Narrowing the case-study registry down to AAPL's own history.

steps.title: The measured edge report
steps.narration: Further down the page, the Edge Report compares three trading strategies over every recorded event window — the honest scorecard for whether any of this actually works.
steps.point_out: It starts computing automatically the moment the page loads. With the operator's 11 real recorded market-data windows now on the books, this is the first run with real data behind it — though as a genuine, uncached, from-scratch computation it can take hours to fully resolve, so what's captured here is its correctly-started, honestly-loading state, not the final numbers.

steps.title: Open the pinned AAPL case study
steps.narration: This row is the pinned AAPL test from June 22, 2026 — a real touch of its ~$300 resistance band, marked rejected. Clicking it starts a genuine replay of the real recorded tick data behind this exact event.
steps.point_out: A drill-in panel opens below the table with a loading indicator.

steps.title: Real recorded tape now backs this event
steps.narration: Here is that drill-in panel, mid-computation.
steps.point_out: The animated loading skeleton confirms a real computation is under way over real recorded tick data, not a synthetic placeholder. It resolves — typically within about fifteen minutes, since nothing here is cached — to a five-state tape timeline of hundreds of real entries tracking buyer control, seller control, and absorption around the touch. This pinned event used to show "No recorded tape for this event."; now it shows the real tape.

steps.title: Back to the cockpit
steps.narration: One last check back at the cockpit, to confirm nothing about live trading data has changed.

steps.title: Confirm Live mode stays untouched
steps.narration: Switching to Live mode with a real symbol.

steps.title: Watch AAPL live
steps.narration: Typing AAPL into the symbol field again, this time for the live feed.

steps.title: Live mode: its own dedicated view
steps.narration: Live mode always uses its own real-time monitoring view.
steps.point_out: The price-chart and band overlay from Simulated and Historical modes are completely absent here — Live mode stays a pure real-time tape reader, never anything trade-related.
